title: Encode IRC §32(i)(2) disqualified income; replace the opaque eitc_relevant_investment_income input

labels.name: pe-parity
labels.description: Mirrors a PolicyEngine policy change; dispatch-ready encode queued

body:
## Encoding debt

`us/statutes/26/32.yaml` gates the EITC on §32(i) in rule `eitc_investment_income_eligible` (lines 627–651, `source: 26 USC 32(i), 32(j)`, one version, `effective_from: '2026-01-01'`):

```
eitc_relevant_investment_income <= eitc_maximum_investment_income
```

Only the threshold is encoded. It is imported from `us:policies/irs/rev-proc-2025-32/earned-income-credit#eitc_maximum_investment_income` (12,200). The other side, `eitc_relevant_investment_income`, is not a rule anywhere in rulespec-us: it resolves to a free input, and the fixtures supply it directly (`us/statutes/26/32.test.yaml:30` and `:192`; `us/statutes/26/24/d.test.yaml:37`, `:111`, `:181` and `:246`). So the §32(i)(2) aggregate is asserted rather than encoded.

The same gap appears in three more places:

- **Rev. Proc. page.** `us/policies/irs/rev-proc-2025-32/page-15.yaml` rule `earned_income_credit_investment_income_eligibility` compares a bare input, `aggregate_investment_income`, with the limit. Nothing imports it.
- **California.** `us-ca/statutes/rtc/17052.yaml` encodes `investment_income_limit` (3,400, `source: 17052(d)`). It defers the final credit, which would need the same aggregate.
- **New Jersey.** `us-nj/statutes/54a:4-7.yaml` rule `age_modified_nj_earned_income_tax_credit_eligible` takes `resident_individual_meets_all_federal_eitc_qualifications_except_age` as an input. That input depends on this aggregate. `54a:4-7.test.yaml` also has no case that is age-ineligible and fails another federal qualification, where the expected result is `not_holds`. See PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9634 for the PolicyEngine side.

**What the search did and didn't find** (rulespec-us `origin/main` `54d90a725`):

- No `us/statutes/26/32/i*` path exists in RuleSpec v1 on `main` or on any of the 688 remote branches.
- No rule computes any of (i)(2)(A)–(E). A grep for `disqualified income`, `32(i)`, `32/i`, `royalt` and `passive` hits:
  - the 32.yaml summary and proof text, and the page-15 gate;
  - `us/statutes/26/61.yaml` (royalties; the §61 inclusion that #1159 named as a blocker);
  - `us/statutes/26/55.yaml` (passive);
  - the NIIT (§1411) and §58 modules;
  - state income-tax pipelines in `us-nj`, `us-pa` and `us-co`;
  - SNAP, TANF and `us-al` DHR modules.
- `us/statutes/26/24/d.yaml:186` is the only importer of `us:statutes/26/32` (`#eitc`, for the §24(d) Social Security tax excess). At least 22 state directories take the federal EITC or its eligibility as a supplied input, including `us-co`, `us-nj`, `us-oh` (`statutes/5747/71`) and `us-va` (`statutes/58.1/58/1-339/8`). They inherit whatever supplies that number.
- All 18 `rulespec-us-*` repos are archived: al, ar, az, ca, co, de, fl, ga, id, ma, md, nc, nh, ny, ok, sc, tn and tx. Their content lives in `rulespec-us/us-<st>/`.

**Prior attempts:**

- Closed PR #1159 encoded only the (i)(1) threshold and deferred the aggregate. Its branch `closure/w4-eitc-32i-invest` names the blockers: §61 category inclusion, §469 missing from the pinned corpus, and the §32(c)(2)/§1402(a) overlap.
- Eleven branches carry legacy `.rac` files for `statute/26/32/i*`, for example `encode-eitc-32` from 2026-03-09. They use a `Person` entity and are neither RuleSpec v1 nor signed.

## Why this matters

1. **PolicyEngine-US had this bug and fixed it on 2026-09-23.**
   - In policyengine-us ≤ 2.10.0 the variable was `net_investment_income + tax_exempt_interest_income - loss_limited_net_capital_gains + max(0, net_capital_gains)`. The NIIT base inside it adds `rental_income` and `passive_partnership_s_corp_income` unfloored.
   - PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9572 (closes PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9567, first released in 2.10.1) splits the calculation into floored baskets.
   - Engine output, which illustrates the issue but is not evidence of the law: a single filer with two children, TY2025, wages 20,000, interest 12,500 and a rental or passive loss of 10,000. PE-US 2.6.17 gives disqualified income 2,500 and EITC 7,152; PE-US 2.15.1 gives 12,500 and EITC 0.
   - Remaining PolicyEngine gaps are in PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9635: dependents' amounts, passive income that is also earned income, and farm rental.
2. **Axiom's oracle projections still net rental losses.** This is tracked in TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-oracles#562.
   - `axiom_oracles/bridges/tax_populace.py:2337` and `adapters/axiom/tax_projection.py:3542-3553` (axiom-oracles `5d7b06e2e`) add `rental_income` unfloored and omit passive partnership and S-corp income. `tax_projection` also has no tax-exempt interest, and the bridge sums dependents.
   - axiom-encode `validator_pipeline.py:40616` (`_PE_US_TAX_UNIT_OVERRIDE_INPUTS`) overrides PolicyEngine's own variable with this projected value. PE-oracle validation of §32 therefore never exercises PolicyEngine's computation.
3. **TAXSIM follows a different rule (engine behavior, not law).**
   - The NBER `taxsimtest` binary (build `cd2026081819`, TY2025, single, two children) counts `scorp` as EITC earned income in both directions:
     - wages 20,000 plus `scorp` −10,000 gives EITC 4,000, which is 40% × 10,000;
     - `scorp` −30,000 gives 0;
     - wages 5,000 plus `scorp` 10,000 gives 6,000, which is 40% × 15,000.
   - Its exclusion of `scorp` from disqualified income is consistent with (E)(i)'s earned-income parenthetical, given that choice. But TAXSIM's own documentation defines the field as "Passive business income … subject to the passive loss limitation", and S-corp pass-through income is not net earnings from self-employment under §1402(a).
   - This is the household-109088 context in PolicyEngine/policyengine-taxsim#1053 and draft PolicyEngine/policyengine-taxsim#1199.

Until (i)(2) is encoded, Axiom cannot adjudicate any of these.

## Statute (verbatim, pinned corpus)

The source is axiom-corpus `data/corpus/provisions/us/statute/2026-07-13-recovery-r2026-07-15-self-contained-r2026-07-17-dedup.jsonl`:

- rows `us/statute/26/32/i` (line 283), `/i/1` (line 1038) and `/i/2` (line 1039); there are no rows below paragraph level;
- source USLM `usc26-section-32.xml`, "Online@119-100";
- in the pinned release `us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap`, and byte-identical at pinned `axiom_corpus_ref` `8f7d60aac` (`.axiom/workflow-toolchain.toml`) and at `main`.

It matches the OLRC text ("laws in effect on September 24, 2026") apart from quote and dash glyphs.

**Scope.** Paragraph (2) defines disqualified income "for purposes of paragraph (1)", which denies the §32(a) credit to "the taxpayer" whose aggregate disqualified income exceeds the limit.

> **(1) In general** No credit shall be allowed under subsection (a) for the taxable year if the aggregate amount of disqualified income of the taxpayer for the taxable year exceeds $10,000.
>
> **(2) Disqualified income** For purposes of paragraph (1), the term “disqualified income” means—
> (A) interest or dividends to the extent includible in gross income for the taxable year,
> (B) interest received or accrued during the taxable year which is exempt from tax imposed by this chapter,
> (C) the excess (if any) of— (i) gross income from rents or royalties not derived in the ordinary course of a trade or business, over (ii) the sum of— (I) the deductions (other than interest) which are clearly and directly allocable to such gross income, plus (II) interest deductions properly allocable to such gross income,
> (D) the capital gain net income (as defined in section 1222) of the taxpayer for such taxable year, and
> (E) the excess (if any) of— (i) the aggregate income from all passive activities for the taxable year (determined without regard to any amount included in earned income under subsection (c)(2) or described in a preceding subparagraph), over (ii) the aggregate losses from all passive activities for the taxable year (as so determined).
> For purposes of subparagraph (E), the term “passive activity” has the meaning given such term by section 469.

(C) and (E) are each "the excess (if any) of" one amount over another, so each is floored at zero on its own. (A), (B) and (D) are separate addends. Nothing in (2) lets a shortfall in (C) or (E) reduce another subparagraph.

**(D).** §1222(9), corpus row `us/statute/26/1222` (jsonl line 56):

> (9) Capital gain net income The term “capital gain net income” means the excess of the gains from sales or exchanges of capital assets over the losses from such sales or exchanges.

`us/statutes/26/1222.yaml` exists, but only with a legacy `applied-rulespec/v1` manifest. `existing_signed_imports_json` accepts only signed-v5 modules (`prepare_signed_backfill.py`, `parse_existing_signed_imports`). So it cannot be imported in a signed dispatch today; see step 1.

**Amount.** Rev. Proc. 2025-32 §3.06(2), corpus row `us/guidance/irs/rev-proc-2025-32/page-15` (in the pinned release):

> (2) Excessive Investment Income. For taxable years beginning in 2026, the earned income tax credit is not allowed under § 32(i) if the aggregate amount of certain investment income exceeds $12,200.

**§469 (for (E)) is not in the pinned release.**

- Rows `us/statute/26/469` and `/103` exist only in axiom-corpus version `2026-09-13-tax-statute-closure-31-title-26`.
- The releases that carry that version are:
  - `us-rulespec-2026-09-13-cms-state-plans-union`
  - `us-rulespec-2026-09-13-federal-and-plans-union`
  - `us-rulespec-2026-09-14-wave4-union`
  - `us-rulespec-2026-09-14-wave4-r2-union`

  `us-rulespec-2026-09-13-followup-union` does not.
- #1389 ("Stage validator fingerprints for the canada-338 corpus union re-pin", open) changes only `validation_waiver_set_sha256`, and its target release does not include §469.

OLRC 26 USC 469, (c) "Passive activity defined":

> (2) Passive activity includes any rental activity
> Except as provided in paragraph (7), the term "passive activity" includes any rental activity.

OLRC 26 USC 469, (j) "Other definitions and special rules":

> (8) Rental activity
> The term "rental activity" means any activity where payments are principally for the use of tangible property.

## Open point: does rental real estate go in (C) or (E)?

This issue does not decide the question.

- **Statute.** On its text, rents "not derived in the ordinary course of a trade or business" go in (C), which is floored alone, and (E)(i)/(ii) exclude amounts "described in a preceding subparagraph".
- **IRS worksheet.** Pub 596 routes all passive Schedule E line 26 rental real estate into the passive basket, and puts only royalties and non-business personal-property rentals in the (C)-like basket.

IRS Pub. 596 (2025), PDF page 7, "Worksheet 1. Investment Income" ("Use this worksheet to figure investment income for the EIC when you file Form 1040 or 1040-SR"). Source: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p596.pdf, sha256 `29e8c669…1dbf`, `pdftotext -layout`. Dot leaders are removed.

> Royalties and Rental Income From Personal Property
> 8. Enter any royalty income from Schedule E (Form 1040), line 23b, plus any income from the rental of personal property shown on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 8l
> 9. Enter any expenses from Schedule E (Form 1040), line 20, related to royalty income, plus any expenses from the rental of personal property deducted on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 24b
> 10. Subtract the amount on line 9 of this worksheet from the amount on line 8. (If the result is less than zero, enter -0-.)
> Passive Activities
> 11. Enter the total of any net income from passive activities (such as income included on Schedule E, line 26, 29a (col. (h)), 34a (col. (d)), or 40; or an ordinary gain on Form 4797, line 10). (See instructions below for lines 11 and 12.)
> 12. Enter the total of any losses from passive activities (such as losses included on Schedule E, line 26, 29b (col. (g)), 34b (col. (c)), or 40; or an ordinary loss on Form 4797, line 10). (See instructions below for lines 11 and 12.)
> 13. Combine the amounts on lines 11 and 12 of this worksheet. (If the result is less than zero, enter -0-.)
>
> Instructions for lines 11 and 12. In figuring the amount to enter on lines 11 and 12, don’t take into account any royalty income (or loss) included on line 26 of Schedule E or any income (or loss) included in your earned income or on line 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, or 10 of this worksheet. To find out if the income on line 26 or line 40 of Schedule E is from a passive activity, see the Schedule E instructions. If any of the rental real estate income (or loss) included on Schedule E, line 26, isn’t from a passive activity, enter “NPA” and the amount of that income (or loss) on the dotted line next to line 26.

**Years.** The TY2021–TY2025 editions have the same line 8–13 structure. The changes are:

- the limit: $10,000, $10,300, $11,000, $11,600, $11,950;
- the Schedule 1 personal-property reference, 8k → 8l;
- the Form 1040 capital-gain reference, 7 → 7a;
- the TY2021 "FPA"/"PAL" labels on Form 4797 line 10, dropped in 2025;
- wording.

PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9572 follows the worksheet.

**Where the two readings differ.** They differ in three situations:

- positive rental real estate income alongside passive losses from another activity (test H1);
- a rental real estate net loss alongside positive passive income from another activity (test H2);
- non-passive ("NPA") rentals that are not a trade or business.

Resolve this with extracted primary evidence (regulations, legislative history, or IRS guidance stating a legal basis) before encoding the rental routing. Engine behavior does not settle it.

## Current encoding path (read 2026-09-26; nothing was run)

- **Signed encoder only.**
  - Content comes from axiom-encode `.github/workflows/targeted-signed-reencode.yml`.
  - Its `production-signing` environment requires reviewers MaxGhenis or PavelMakarchuk.
  - It runs `--backend openai` with `OPENAI_API_KEY` (workflow lines 1228 and 1309).
  - Hand-written RuleSpec is rejected by the generated-guard.
- **Encoder pin.**
  - `.axiom/workflow-toolchain.toml` moved to `06b01708` / 0.2.2049 in #1392, and axiom-encode `main` is `06b01708`, so a dispatch now would bind.
  - Manifests are bound to the running pinned encoder (`cli.py:22672-22680`), so the next axiom-encode merge reopens the mismatch.
- **Local supervised encoder.**
  - The 2026-09-25 root install is `/opt/axiom-verification-dynamics-394663ca`, with axiom-encode 0.2.2007.
  - It is not usable for this repo as installed: 0.2.2007 is not the pinned 0.2.2049, and the CLI requires an attached broker (`cli.py:26656`, `toolchain.py:264`).
- **`32.yaml` is under a validation waiver.** `known-validation-gaps.yaml` `validate_failures` has an entry for it (fingerprint `sha256:ea9c23c2…`, expires 2026-12-21, under the generic tracker #782). Open draft #1363 also edits it. So step 1 is a new file.
- **Not blocked by #1399.** Paragraph (i)(2) has no filing-status dependence.

## Plan

### Step 1. Encode a new module, `us/statutes/26/32/i.yaml`

Encode it for corpus citation `us/statute/26/32/i`, which is in the pinned release. Precedents for a subsection citation are `us/statutes/7/2015/f.yaml` (`us/statute/7/2015/f`) and #1403's `us/statutes/26/32/d` plan. The existing `us/statutes/26/32/c/2.yaml` uses the section-level citation, so either granularity has precedent. `review_finding`:

> Encode 26 USC 32(i) (corpus us/statute/26/32/i, /i/1, /i/2) as its own module at us/statutes/26/32/i.yaml. us/statutes/26/32.yaml carries the (i)(2) aggregate as the opaque input `eitc_relevant_investment_income`. This module must compute "disqualified income" from its five subparagraphs so 32.yaml can import it later. Do not import us:statutes/26/32. Entity TaxUnit. Every amount is the taxpayer's own (both spouses on a joint return), not a dependent's.
>
> Required outputs, each with verbatim proof excerpts from the corpus provision:
>
> 1. (A) Money: interest and dividends to the extent includible in gross income (leaf inputs scoped exactly so). Do NOT reuse the NIIT names `taxable_interest_income` / `dividend_income` / `rental_income` / `royalty_income`, which are declared as post-classification §1411(c)(1)(A) amounts (#1231).
> 2. (B) Money: interest received or accrued during the taxable year which is exempt from chapter 1 tax (leaf input).
> 3. (C) Money: max(0, gross income from rents or royalties not derived in the ordinary course of a trade or business − (allocable non-interest deductions + allocable interest deductions)). The floor applies to (C) alone.
> 4. (D) Money: a leaf input scoped exactly to "the capital gain net income (as defined in section 1222) of the taxpayer", declared as a deferred dependency on us:statutes/26/1222#capital_gain_net_income until that module has a signed-v5 manifest. Alternatively, co-encode us/statute/26/1222 in the same source bundle.
> 5. (E) Money: max(0, aggregate passive-activity income − aggregate passive-activity losses), both determined without regard to amounts included in earned income under 32(c)(2) or described in (A)–(D). §469 is not in the pinned corpus, so take the two aggregates as leaf inputs stating exactly that scope and declare §469 as a deferred dependency.
> 6. `eitc_disqualified_income` (Money) = (A) + (B) + (C) + (D) + (E).

### Step 2. Oracle coverage and projection

- Run `axiom-encode oracle-coverage-pending sync` for the new outputs (precedent: #1381).
- Fix the projection in TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-oracles#562.

### Step 3. Rewire §32

Do this after #1363, in the same wave as #1403 (32/d) and #1397 (page-15 repoint):

- Pass `existing_signed_imports_json=["us/statutes/26/32/i.yaml"]`.
- Replace `eitc_relevant_investment_income` with the imported `eitc_disqualified_income`.
- Retire the waiver.
- Give `page-15.yaml` `aggregate_investment_income` the same treatment when it is re-encoded.
- Update every consumer of the old input name:
  - rulespec-us fixtures `32.test.yaml` and `24/d.test.yaml`;
  - axiom-encode `validator_pipeline.py:40616` and `tests/test_policyengine_ecps_tax.py:839-856`;
  - axiom-oracles `tests/test_axiom_tax_projection.py` and `tests/bridges/test_policyengine_tax_populace.py`;
  - axiom-corpus `src/axiom_corpus/concepts/data/us.yaml:10613` and `:16964`;
  - axiom-corpus legacy `src/axiom_corpus/verifier.py:87` and `:221-224`.
- Add the NJ companion case: age-ineligible and over the investment-income limit, expected `not_holds`.

### Step 4. Historical years

TY2021–TY2025 limits are $10,000, $10,300, $11,000, $11,600 and $11,950 (Pub 596 Worksheet 1 line 15). They need those years' Rev. Proc. amounts. The OLRC amendment notes show (i)(2)(D)–(E) came from Pub. L. 104-193 (1996), and Pub. L. 117-2 changed only (i)(1). Pre-2026 applicability still needs verification against dated statute text.

## Companion tests

Every expected value is **hand-computed from the §32(i)(2) text quoted above**, with the TY2026 limit of $12,200 from Rev. Proc. 2025-32 §3.06(2). No value comes from an engine. All tests are TY2026, TaxUnit; unlisted amounts are 0, and (D) is set as the step 1 leaf input.

| # | Case | Inputs | (A) | (B) | (C) | (D) | (E) | Total | eligible (≤ 12,200) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | rental loss in (C) | interest 12,500; gross rents 5,000; non-interest deductions 15,000 | 12,500 | 0 | max(0, 5,000 − 15,000) = 0 | 0 | 0 | 12,500 | not_holds |
| A′ | passive loss in (E) | interest 12,500; passive losses 10,000 | 12,500 | 0 | 0 | 0 | max(0, 0 − 10,000) = 0 | 12,500 | not_holds |
| B | netting within (E), eligible | interest 8,000; passive income 5,000; passive losses 3,000 | 8,000 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 2,000 | 10,000 | holds |
| C | capital loss | interest 12,500; (D) 0 (net capital loss) | 12,500 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 12,500 | not_holds |
| D | tax-exempt interest counts | taxable interest 6,000; tax-exempt interest 6,500 | 6,000 | 6,500 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 12,500 | not_holds |
| E1 | royalties net of deductions | interest 4,000; royalties 9,000; non-interest deductions 1,500; allocable interest 500 | 4,000 | 0 | 7,000 | 0 | 0 | 11,000 | holds |
| E2 | royalty loss can't offset interest | interest 12,500; royalties 1,000; non-interest deductions 4,000 | 12,500 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 12,500 | not_holds |
| F | passive income > losses | interest 8,000; passive income 9,000; passive losses 4,000 | 8,000 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 5,000 | 13,000 | not_holds |
| G1 | boundary | interest 7,200; passive income 5,000 | 7,200 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 5,000 | 12,200 | holds ("exceeds" is strict) |
| G2 | boundary + 1 | interest 7,201; passive income 5,000 | 7,201 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 5,000 | 12,201 | not_holds |
| H1 | **blocked on the open point** | interest 8,000; rental real estate rents 5,000; passive S-corp losses 10,000 | 8,000 | 0 | (C)-routing 5,000 | 0 | 0 | (C)-routing 13,000 not_holds; worksheet routing 8,000 holds | add once resolved |
| H2 | **blocked on the open point** | interest 8,000; rents 5,000; rental deductions 15,000; passive S-corp income 8,000 | 8,000 | 0 | (C)-routing 0 | 0 | (C)-routing 8,000 | (C)-routing 16,000 not_holds; worksheet routing (E) max(0, 8,000 − 10,000) = 0, 8,000 holds | add once resolved |

Step 3 adds a flow-through case to `32.test.yaml`: single, two qualifying children, wages 20,000, interest 12,500 and a passive loss of 10,000. Disqualified income is 12,500 > 12,200, so `eitc` is 0 under (i)(1): "No credit shall be allowed".

**Properties the tests should pin, for every input:**

- `eitc_disqualified_income` is non-decreasing in each income input: interest, dividends, tax-exempt interest, gross rents and royalties, capital gain net income, and passive income.
- It is non-increasing in each deduction or loss input.
- (C) ≥ 0 and (E) ≥ 0.
- The total is at least (A) + (B) + (D).
